assertion_audit.assertions: Accepted delivery exists and record_mtime equals the independently set filesystem mtime.
assertion_audit.fails_if: The existing delivery owner refuses valid JSON or substitutes observation time for filesystem time.

assertion_audit.assertions: Exactly one receipt has original file mtime and reviewer identity; source JSON is unchanged; later wrapper filing/re-observation does not alter journal bytes.
assertion_audit.fails_if: Remove the watcher observer, use observation time, misassociate the reviewer, rewrite source content, or append a duplicate on replay.

assertion_audit.assertions: Filing succeeds without refusals and produces one receipt at the original file mtime.
assertion_audit.fails_if: Remove review_file_instant context so note_review_record uses the delayed store clock; the recorded reversal fails :499.

assertion_audit.assertions: Unparsed, scoreless, foreign-review and wrong-head files fail delivery recognition and create no write receipt.
assertion_audit.fails_if: Bypass existing delivery validation in the observer and stamp arbitrary declared files; valid-file positive control above proves the instrument can observe one.

assertion_audit.assertions: Suppressed second-round request yields positive unknown time and an unknown interval; complete two-round history yields zero unknown.
assertion_audit.fails_if: Remove review_admitted from _PAIRED so the earlier round satisfies the later round; the recorded reversal fails :538.

assertion_audit.assertions: The journal request identity equals the dispatched identity and returned/queued identity, fallback pointers are queued, repeat rounds get distinct identities, and complete history has no unknown time.
assertion_audit.fails_if: Stop forwarding receipt_run_id to dispatch or either queue builder, reuse an earlier round identity, omit a request or break stage pairing.

assertion_independence: No vacuous guard found. Timestamp expectations originate from os.utime on the delivered file, not an at argument supplied to record_stage. The direct dispatch mock returns its input ID, so dispatched[-1] == reviewer_id alone is a passthrough assertion; the same chain also compares the independently read journal request attempt, and fallback arms compare the real queued pointer ID. Census cases read persisted receipts and include a suppressed-request negative branch. Passthrough equality is not counted alone as durability.
